description: TypeScript 4.9+: `expr satisfies T` checks that `expr` is assignable to `T` but keeps the inferred type of `expr`.
`const x: T = ...` validates the value and makes `T` the declared type, widening every property to `T`.
`expr as T` overrides the inferred type without checking completeness; it can hide bugs.
Freezes a literal with readonly literal types and still validates it against `T`.
